minutes.headline: Select Board sent Complete Streets alternative one to the state and put a non-binding old primary demolition article on the warrant.
minutes.summary: The board chose which Complete Streets round-two project to submit, then debated old primary school repairs and whether to test Town Meeting sentiment on demolition. It heard about a possible Butterfly Lane road acceptance, adopted a town manager evaluation procedure, and approved placeholder articles for the November special town meeting, including two liquor license petitions.

Explained condo association road and storm drain costs and benefits as they relate to Butterfly Lane.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to submit Complete Streets alternative one to the state, after an earlier motion to submit three items failed 2-3.
The board voted 3-2 to add a non-binding article to the special town meeting warrant offering demolition of the old primary building.
The town manager is to get a cost estimate from the structural inspection of the old primary school; the board did not vote on repairs.
The board accepted the town manager evaluation procedure 4-1 and approved funding for seven architectural preservation district signs.
A hearing on Butterfly Lane road acceptance was set for October 15th, and the board agreed to apply for two liquor license petitions.

why_it_matters: The old primary school's future, whether repaired, sold or demolished, may come to Town Meeting as a vote and could affect taxes, since the town manager said little is left in the facilities maintenance account for projects.

Accepting Butterfly Lane as a town road would put its upkeep, including storm drain cleaning, on the town budget, which is mostly taxes, so the cost estimate the DPW director is gathering bears on that decision.
watch_next: Public comment and social media policies, tabled to October 1.
